      How your work is assessed

      Six assignments
      42%
      Midterm · Data systems
      15%
      Final · Cumulative
      15%
      Capstone · In pairs
      13%
      Five labs
      10%
      Weekly concept checks
      5%

      Exams test reasoning. Practice exams are provided; you may bring one page of notes. Concept checks allow unlimited attempts and are graded for completion.

      Assignment grading +

      Checkpoint: 20% of each assignment. Final submission: 80%, assessed on correctness (~50%), performance (~20%), and analysis (~30%). Performance credit requires correct code. Analysis explains a measured bottleneck and tests a proposed change.

      Late work & outages +

      Five slip days per semester, at most two per submission. Reference outputs are released 48 hours after each deadline; no submissions are accepted after that. No slip days on the capstone. Accommodations and outages are handled separately. Cluster outages near a deadline move the deadline.

      Collaboration & AI tools +

      Discuss ideas freely; write your own code and analysis. Provided code and reference outputs are allowed. Don’t share or view others’ code. Capstone partners may share capstone code; individual assignments stay independent until their deadlines.

      AI may explain concepts, read documentation, and help debug. It may not write the parts each handout assigns to you, including selected Spark jobs, kernel and measurement code, collective logic, or gradient synchronization. Cite AI use, including prompts.

      Code check-offs +

      After D3 and T3, complete a ten-minute individual code walkthrough with staff. Each handout publishes the questions, criteria, and grade weight.

      Help, access & shared resources +

      If you fall behind, start the next stage from a reference output. Attend recitation or office hours for tools and concepts. If you miss a checkpoint, a TA will contact you.

      Register with the Disability Resource Center and speak with an instructor early for accommodations. The Rice Honor Code applies. Test at small scale and release resources when finished; idle jobs count against your allocation. Every graded run fits a guaranteed per-student allocation.
